blind_target.authors: Pennycook G, Cheyne JA, Barr N, Koehler DJ, Fugelsang JA.
blind_target.title: Cognitive style and religiosity: The role of conflict detection.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Furthermore, in light of prior evidence linking the need for cognition (NFC) and religiosity [ 11 ], we also included a measure of need for cognition (NFC) at the end of the study to allow for exploratory analyses probing the relationship between NFC and religious beliefs; these analyses yielded additional support for the measurement order hypothesis.
blind_target.outcome_quote: These patterns mirror findings reported by Pennycook et al. (Study 1) [ 11 ]. When participants completed the religious beliefs measures first, however, NFC was no longer correlated with any of the religious beliefs measures: intrinsic religiosity r (205) = .06, p = .394; intuitive religious beliefs r (205) = .06, p = .384; belief in supernatural agents r (205) = .03, p = .647.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Explicit exploratory re-test of NFC/religiosity relationship agrees under analytic-first order and fails under reversed order. The reference prints 2013 (despite volume issue metadata suggesting a later issue).

luna_triage.reason: Results directly compare the measured NFC–religiosity correlations with Pennycook et al. Study 1 and state that the patterns mirror that work. The only supplied shipped row is Gervais and Norenzayan (2012), a distinct analytic-thinking intervention study, not Pennycook et al. 2013.
luna_triage.omission_quote: These patterns mirror findings reported by Pennycook et al. (Study 1) [ 11 ].
